newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DAVIES DROP-GOAL FLATTENS WASPS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DAVIES DROP-GOAL FLATTENS WASPS.

text.p: Former Welsh captain Jonathan Davies saved his best until last to earn Cardiff a crucial 26-24 victory over Wasps in their opening match in European Cup pool D on Sunday.

Davies had endured a woeful day with the boot, missing five of his seven attempts at goal, in contrast to Canadian fly-half Gareth Rees who kicked his eighth penalty from nine attempts to put his side 24-23 ahead with less than two minutes remaining.

But Davies, who still harbours ambitions of further Welsh caps having returned to union from rugby league, kept cool when it mattered to land a 79th minute drop-goal, his second of the game, to repay a large chunk of his big transfer fee.
The Welsh side, finalists last year, featured 14 internationals and fully deserved to win.
They scored three tries to nil, two of them from test scrum- half Robert Howley, although strict refereeing from Irish official Brian Stirling threatened to negate their forward domination.
Rees landed eight successive kicks, five of them in the first-half, but Wasps were mostly a disappointment in a match they sorely needed to win.
Former All Black Va'aiga Tuigamamla had a quiet day in the Wasps' midfield and the home side will require a much-improved performance when Toulouse visit London in a fortnight.
